haiku-low.q1: Only on-call running the failover command starts it. Detection (2 of 3 probes, 3 failures in a row) just pages on-call and never starts a failover.
haiku-low.q2: It stops before fencing, leaving A untouched. It continues only if on-call repeats the command with the explicit accept-data-loss override.
haiku-low.q3: Before promoting B's database: A fenced (active=B set, lease wait finished). Before B's workers start: database promoted. Before DNS moves: B's app passes its health check.
haiku-low.q4: B's Redis starts empty, so every signed-in user must sign in again. This is accepted.
haiku-low.q5: It stays fenced and is never reused as primary. It is rebuilt as a replica of B; moving back is a separate planned switchover.
haiku-low.q6: A's apps and workers hold a short lease on active=A, renewed from the control store. They stop writing when renewal fails or the record says B.
haiku-low.q7: The control store holds the active-region record. The failover command writes it (active=B, then final), and A's apps and workers read it to renew their lease. Other readers: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: The command sets every running job in B's copy to pending. Jobs must be safe to run twice, since they may have partly run in A. Jobs lost in the last seconds are gone.
haiku-low.q9: Run the command again: it takes the lock (on-call can release a stale one), reads the run log, and resumes at the first unfinished step. Abort is allowed only before step 6, which sets active=A and releases the lock.
haiku-low.q10: Users move to B within about a minute, given the 60 s TTL. Cached-DNS client behavior beyond that is NOT STATED. Signed-in users must sign in again.
haiku-low.q11: Loss is limited by the 30 s RPO: the lag check stops failover if B's last recorded lag exceeds 30 s, unless on-call accepts data loss. Unsent writes are lost.

sonnet.q1: Only on-call running the failover command starts a failover. Detection (2 of 3 probes each see 3 consecutive failures) just pages on-call and never starts a failover by itself; no automatic promotion exists.
sonnet.q2: If last recorded replay lag is over 30 s, the command stops (read-only check, A untouched). It continues only if on-call repeats it with the explicit accept-data-loss override.
sonnet.q3: Before promoting B's DB: step 5 (fencing A: active = B set, and a full lease period waited) must be finished (and the lag check passed or overridden). Before B's workers start: the DB promotion (step 6) must have made the database writable. Before DNS moves: B's app must pass the health check (step 9).
sonnet.q4: Sessions are lost. Redis in each region is separate and not replicated; B's Redis starts empty, so every signed-in user must sign in again (accepted).
sonnet.q5: It stays fenced and is never reused as primary. A is rebuilt as a replica of B; moving back is a separate planned switchover, not part of this plan.
sonnet.q6: The fence: A's apps and workers hold a short lease on active = A that they renew from the control store. If renewal fails (can't reach the store) or the record says B, they stop all writes. The command waited one full lease period after setting active = B, so A has either seen the change or lost its lease, with no contact with A needed.
sonnet.q7: The control store (outside both regions' failure domains) holds the active-region record. The failover command writes it (active = B at fencing and again as final at step 10; active = A on abort before step 6). A's apps and workers read/renew their lease from it and stop writes if it fails or says B.
sonnet.q8: They remain marked running in B's copy of the table. Step 7 sets every running row to pending so B's workers re-run them. Jobs must be idempotent since they may have partly run in A. Jobs created in the lost last seconds of data are gone (within RPO).
sonnet.q9: Run the command again: it takes the lock (on-call can release a stale lock from a dead run), reads the run log and resumes at the first step not marked done; steps are safe to repeat. Going back to A is possible only if aborting before step 6 (promotion): the command sets active = A and releases the lock, and A renews its lease and resumes. After step 6, abort is not allowed; only forward.
sonnet.q10: NOT STATED beyond the DNS TTL: the DNS name has a 60 s TTL and users move to B within about a minute. The document does not say what a client with stale cached DNS experiences.
sonnet.q11: Up to the writes A had not yet sent to B, limited by the RPO of 30 s: the lag check on B's last recorded replay lag (usually under 5 s) must be 30 s or less, unless on-call overrides with accept-data-loss, in which case more can be lost.
